summary: Interim report, investigation ongoing. web-01: the site plugin file wp-content/plugins/larkspur-site/inc/rental-quote.php was hand-copied and is not in the git repo. It contained a hidden branch: a secret 'ref' token returned the wp-config DB credentials, and a 'code' parameter let the caller test DB passwords. 70.120.249.96 used it on Oct 30 (the response size matches a credentials dump) and on Nov 10. 98.97.180.246 used it on Nov 1 and Nov 11. All of these requests came with no referrer. Actions: I removed the backdoor branch and kept the normal price quote working (original saved in /root/ir). I rotated app-db-password and updated the other copy in /etc/larkspur/report.cnf; the site and the report login both work. I also removed mu-plugins/agency-support.php, an old 2019 Blue Ridge Web Co plugin that allowed unauthenticated command execution via ?asup=purge&path=. 174.205.78.165 POSTed to / today at 16:14 and got a 159-byte reply, likely that plugin's environment dump. Still checking db-01, ci-01 and the other weaknesses.

COMPROMISE: web-01 had a backdoor in the site plugin. inc/rental-quote.php was hand-copied (it is not in the git repo on ci-01). A secret 'ref' value made it return the wp-config DB credentials, and a 'code' parameter let the caller test DB passwords against db-01. 70.120.249.96 used it on Oct 30; the 247-byte reply matches a credentials dump. It came back on Nov 10, and 98.97.180.246, with the same browser string and the same pattern (direct POST, no referrer), came on Nov 1 and Nov 11. Neither IP ever logged in by SSH to any server. I found no sign of shell access, persistence or use of the stolen credentials, and db-01 only accepts connections from the office network.

CONTAINMENT/ROTATION: I removed the backdoor branch; the normal price quote still works and the original is kept in /root/ir. I rotated app-db-password and updated the extra copy in /etc/larkspur/report.cnf; the site, the orders/report jobs and the report login were tested OK. The wp_larkspur DB account now only accepts logins from 10.20.0.10, not the whole 10.20.0.0/24.

WEAKNESSES FIXED:
- Removed wp-content/mu-plugins/agency-support.php, an old 2019 Blue Ridge Web Co plugin. It allowed unauthenticated command execution as www-data via ?asup=purge&path=. 174.205.78.165 got what looks like its environment dump today at 16:14. Switchback's 'SwitchbackSupport' POSTs to / were probably using it; they will need another way to purge the cache (each release already flushes it).
- nginx now refuses to run .php files under wp-content/uploads.
- Removed deploy's 'sudo rsync' rule on web-01 (in /etc/sudoers.d/larkspur). It amounted to full root, and CI doesn't use it; larkspur-deploy and larkspur-restart are unchanged.
- Locked the jpark account on web-01 and ci-01 and removed it from sudo on web-01. jpark is not in the staff list and was being brute-forced.
- On ci-01, the backups account (which receives the DB archives) also accepted the CI deploy key. It now accepts only db-01's key, and only from 10.20.0.20. Tested: db-01 can still deliver.
- Removed Maria's MacBook key from rnakamura's account (db-01) and tbrooks's account (ci-01). It had never been used there; Maria's own accounts are unchanged.

NOT AN INTRUSION, IN MY VIEW: 54.36.199.108 logs in as deploy with the password every few hours across all 14 days of logs: no failures, no sudo, short command sessions. That matches the 'old monitoring box' that rotate-secret lists as holding the deploy password. Please confirm.

LEFT FOR MARIA:
- Password SSH is enabled everywhere, including for deploy from the internet.
- Grafana (3000) and node_exporter (9100) are open to the public.
- larkspur-mailing-export writes as root into users' home folders. A user could use a symlink to make it overwrite other files as root.
- The ci-01 maint job has a 'site' mode that would run, as root, a script that deploy/www-data can edit. It is set to 'local' (off) now.

Payment key, offsite key, deploy password and the root secrets were not rotated: I saw no sign that they were read. If the payment key is ever rotated, the copy in db-01 /etc/larkspur/gateway.env must be updated too; for the offsite key, the copy in db-01 /root/.config/larkspur/offsite.env.

COMPROMISE (web-01): wp-content/plugins/larkspur-site/inc/rental-quote.php was hand-copied (it is not in the git repo on ci-01) and contained a backdoor. A secret 'ref' value made it return the wp-config DB credentials, and a 'code' parameter let the caller test DB passwords against db-01. 70.120.249.96 used it on Oct 30; the 247-byte reply matches a credentials dump. It came back on Nov 10, and 98.97.180.246, with the same browser string and the same direct POSTs with no referrer, came on Nov 1 and Nov 11. Since my fix, 172.56.216.189 has been POSTing to the same file every 2–3 minutes and gets only normal quotes. It is possibly the same actor checking whether the backdoor still works. None of these IPs ever logged in by SSH to any server, and I found no persistence, shell access or use of the stolen credentials. db-01 only accepts the office network.

CONTAINMENT AND ROTATION:
- Removed the backdoor branch; the price quote still works. The original is kept in /root/ir on web-01.
- Rotated app-db-password and updated the extra copy in /etc/larkspur/report.cnf.
- The wp_larkspur DB account now only accepts logins from web-01 (10.20.0.10).
- I didn't rotate the payment key, offsite key, deploy password or the root secrets: I saw no sign they were read. If you rotate the payment key later, also update db-01 /etc/larkspur/gateway.env; for the offsite key, db-01 /root/.config/larkspur/offsite.env.

WEAKNESSES FIXED:
- Removed mu-plugins/agency-support.php (Blue Ridge Web Co, 2019), which allowed unauthenticated command execution via the asup/path parameters. 174.205.78.165 got its environment dump at 16:14 and tried again at 16:26 (no longer works). Switchback's 'SwitchbackSupport' cache-purge POSTs no longer do anything; each release already flushes the cache.
- nginx: .php under uploads is denied, and xmlrpc.php is blocked.
- Removed deploy's sudo rsync rule on web-01, which amounted to full root.
- jpark (not in the staff list): locked on web-01 and ci-01 and removed from sudo. In WordPress, demoted from administrator to subscriber, password reset and sessions ended.
- ci-01: the backups account accepts only db-01's key, and only from 10.20.0.20 (it also accepted the CI deploy key).
- Removed Maria's MacBook key from the rnakamura (db-01) and tbrooks (ci-01) accounts; it had never been used there.
- The internal maint.d script is now root-owned; ci-01 would run it as root in 'site' mode.
- larkspur-mailing-export now writes the CSV as the requesting user, so a symlink can no longer turn it into a root write.

VERIFIED WORKING AFTER CHANGES: site pages and quotes, releases every 3 minutes (latest 16:30 ok), dumps reaching ci-01 (16:30 ok), offsite copy, payouts check, orders/report/stock jobs, and the 16:31 settlement batch (10 payouts sent).

JUDGED LEGITIMATE, PLEASE CONFIRM:
- 54.36.199.108 logs in as deploy with the password a few times a day across all 14 days of logs: no failures, no sudo, short sessions. It looks like the old monitoring box.
- Theo's laptop key was used at 16:24 from a new IP, 67.180.176.27, 38 seconds after use from his home IP. The commands were routine.

STILL OPEN: password SSH is enabled everywhere, including deploy from the internet; Grafana (3000) and node_exporter (9100) are open to the public.
